projects.budget_note: RAISED 2026-10-07 to 36/day (was 12) by the dev seat. MEASURED REASON: at 12 wakes a day and a ~25 minute shift, a project gets under five hours of work a day, and kosher-ai-filter's own roadmap now holds 20 filed todo items against 47 unchecked boxes in its docs (18 of them mapped to runnable definitions of done) - a project that needs weeks of work would take months at 12/day. The limits that actually bound this are unchanged and still enforced by the store, not by this file: WAKE_MAX_PER_SOURCE_PER_HOUR (12/hour/worker), the 500/day release backstop, and the 25.00 USD/day spend ceiling against a measured 0.036-0.068 USD per release, so 36 releases is about 2.45 USD; if every one of the 9 enabled projects used its whole 36 the system ceiling (25.00 USD/day, written once in wake.py DEFAULT_MAX_USD_PER_DAY) still binds first at about 22 USD, so this file cannot raise the real ceiling. Owner's standing instruction behind the earlier raise still applies: 'There's no reason to limit how much you could do per day... The point of stopping you isn't to make you do less work is to make sure you're not doing stupid work or doing the same work over and over. Or wasting money.' Dedup by subject and the ledger's own title dedup are what stop repetition; the count is only a runaway backstop.

projects.shift_packet_note: CANARY 2026-10-01 (LEDGER #172, attempt 479): this project's wake prompt is the generated shift packet (~/bin/shift-packet.py) instead of the 19 KB standing contract. Set "shift_packet": false to go back with no code change; PROJECT_KEEPALIVE_SHIFT_PACKET=0 forces the legacy contract for every project. The packet never renders a prompt that is empty or lacks its END FROZEN PREFIX marker - on any failure project-keepalive.py falls back to the literal contract. shift_packet_cutover is the mtime of the file change that made the packet live (not a guessed time), to be passed to `shift-packet.py --shifts-median --cutover` once 10 shifts have run after it.
